title: The stability of electronic Poiseuille flow in two-dimensional materials
authors: Marine Bastida, Alvaro Meseguer, Iacopo Torre
abstract: Motivated by the experimental observation of electronic Poiseuille flow in graphene [J.A. Sulpizio et al. Nature 576, 75 (2019)] we analyze the linear stability of plane-Poiseuille flow of electrons in a two-dimensional material using a modified Orr-Sommerfeld equation. We calculate the critical current needed to make the flow unstable as a function of the experimental parameters and characterize the most favorable situation, that is the one needing the lowest current density, to observe flow instability. We predict the streamwise wavenumber and frequency at which the instability occurs and discuss the difficulties of an experiment aimed at probing this phenomenon.
summary: This paper investigates when electronic Poiseuille flow in 2D materials becomes unstable using linear stability theory. By solving a modified Orr-Sommerfeld equation, the authors determine the minimum current density required to induce turbulence. The findings pinpoint optimal geometric conditions for observing this fundamental fluid dynamic instability in nanoscale electronics.
main_problem: The study analyzes the linear stability of electronic Poiseuille flow within two-dimensional materials.
main_result: The instability onset is characterized by a minimum critical current density required for turbulence, which occurs at specific geometric ratios ($W \approx 2D$).
method: Linear stability analysis using a modified Orr-Sommerfeld equation derived from the Navier-Stokes equations.
model_or_system: The system models electron flow in a 2D material (like graphene) under plane Poiseuille flow, governed by continuity and a modified Navier-Stokes equation incorporating electrical driving forces.
key_observables: Critical current density ($J_{\min}$), critical Reynolds number ($	ext{Re}_c$), streamwise wavenumber ($k_c$), and frequency ($f_{cr}$).
important_parameters: Channel width to diffusion length ratio ($W/D$) and boundary scattering length ($\ell_B$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes linear perturbations, neglecting non-linear terms; it also uses simplified models for electron interactions (e.g., assuming $\ell_{ee}$ is small).
figures_summary: Figures show velocity profiles for varying geometric ratios and stability diagrams mapping the transition from stable to unstable flow regions as a function of current density.
paper_structure: The paper develops the governing equations, performs linear stability analysis by solving an eigenvalue problem (modified Orr-Sommerfeld equation), and analyzes results in various limiting regimes ($W/D$ ratios).
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics, the mathematical framework of analyzing instabilities via linearized partial differential equations is highly relevant to open quantum systems and non-equilibrium dynamics.
